sections.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes

tracks.title: Welcome — a palace, two barons and seven centuries
tracks.where: In the central hall on Level 0, just inside the entrance from the Paseo del Prado, before you walk to the far end of the hall and go up.
tracks.what: Welcome and how the guide works: the Thyssen-Bornemisza collection, built by Heinrich (1875–1947) and Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza (1921–2002); 1988 loan of 775 works; opened 8 October 1992 in the Palacio de Villahermosa, converted by Rafael Moneo; 1993 purchase by the Spanish State; Carmen Thyssen collection on Level 0. In passing: Tintoretto, Paradise, ca. 1588, oil on canvas, Central hall.
tracks.listen: How a family's private collection became a national museum, how the walk runs from the top of the building down, and how to use the three lengths of this guide.

tracks.title: Room 1 · Duccio di Buoninsegna — Christ and the Samaritan Woman
tracks.where: Room 1, "14th Century. Early Italian Painting", the first room at the top of the stairs. Find the small, almost square gold-ground panel, about 44 by 46 cm: Christ seated on a well, a woman with a pitcher on her head, and a walled city with a gate on the right.
tracks.what: Duccio di Buoninsegna, Christ and the Samaritan Woman, 1310–1311, tempera and gold on panel, 43.5 × 46 cm, inv. 133 (1971.7). Also: Master of the Magdalen, The Virgin and Child enthroned with Saints Dominic and Martin, and two angels, ca. 1290, tempera and gold on panel, 177 × 86.5 cm, Room 1.
tracks.listen: The giant altarpiece Siena carried through its streets, the small scene that came from its back, and the oldest painting in the collection.

tracks.title: Room 2 · Extra · Anonymous German artist active in Konstanz — The Birth of the Virgin
tracks.where: Room 2, "15th Century. German and Spanish Painting". Look for a tall, narrow panel, about 85 by 35 cm: a bedroom with a bed set at a slant, Saint Anne sitting up in it and women busy all around her.
tracks.what: Anonymous German artist, active in Konstanz, ca. 1430, The Birth of the Virgin, ca. 1430, panel, 84.5 × 34.7 cm, inv. 262 (1967.1.1). Also: Joan Mates, Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist with a Donor, ca. 1410, oil on panel, 191 × 121 cm, Room 2.
tracks.listen: A medieval lying-in room, where everyone is working except the new mother, and a Catalan panel that waited centuries for its painter's name.

tracks.title: Room 3 · Jacques Daret — The Nativity
tracks.where: Room 3, "15th Century. Early Netherlandish Painting". Find the nearly square panel, about 60 by 53 cm: a Nativity outside a simple stable, the Christ Child lying on the ground in golden rays, Joseph holding a candle, and a woman in front stretching out her hands.
tracks.what: Jacques Daret, The Nativity (La Adoración del Niño), ca. 1434–35, oil on panel, 59.5 × 53 cm, inv. 124 (1935.17). Also: Follower of Dirck Bouts, The Virgin and Child, ca. 1465, oil on panel, 28.5 × 20 cm, Room 3; Gerard David, The Crucifixion, ca. 1475, oil on panel, 88 × 56 cm, Room 3. Jan van Eyck, The Annunciation Diptych, named only as away on loan.
tracks.listen: The midwife who refused to believe, the candle that the Child's light outshines, and how Van Eyck is still present in a room he has left for the season.

tracks.title: Room 4 · Extra · Bramantino — The Risen Christ
tracks.where: Room 4, "15th Century. Italian Painting". Look for an upright panel, about 109 by 73 cm: a pale Christ facing you to below the waist, wounds in his hands and side, red-rimmed eyes, a dark background and a small river view with a tall-masted ship on the left.
tracks.what: Bramantino (Bartolomeo Suardi), The Risen Christ, ca. 1490, mixed media on panel, 109 × 73 cm, inv. 61 (1937.1). Also: Paolo Uccello, The Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John the Baptist, Saint John the Evangelist and Saint Francis, ca. 1460–1465, tempera on panel, 45 × 67 cm, Room 4.
tracks.listen: A picture that had the wrong painter and the wrong title, and a Christ who has come back from death without any sense of triumph.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 5 · Domenico Ghirlandaio — Portrait of Giovanna degli Albizzi Tornabuoni
tracks.where: Room 5, "15th and 16th Centuries. Renaissance Portraiture". Find the young woman in strict profile, richly dressed, in front of a dark niche holding a jewel, a small book, a string of beads and a little slip of paper with writing: the picture on the cover of the museum map, about 77 by 49 cm.
tracks.what: Domenico Ghirlandaio (Domenico Bigordi), Portrait of Giovanna degli Albizzi Tornabuoni, 1489–1490, mixed media on panel, 77 × 49 cm, inv. 158 (1935.6). Also named: Robert Campin, Portrait of a Stout Man. Robert de Masmines (?), ca. 1425, Room 5; Francesco del Cossa, Portrait of a Man with a Ring, ca. 1472–1477, Room 5.
tracks.listen: The young bride behind the museum's signature image, the debate over whether she was already dead, and how the portrait was born in this room.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 5 · Hans Holbein the Younger — Portrait of Henry VIII of England
tracks.where: Room 5, "15th and 16th Centuries. Renaissance Portraiture". Look for the smallest royal face in the room, a panel only about 28 by 20 cm: Henry VIII square to you, in a flat hat with a jewelled pendant, hands visible below.
tracks.what: Hans Holbein the Younger, Portrait of Henry VIII of England, ca. 1537, oil on panel, 28 × 20 cm, inv. 191 (1934.39). Also: Robert Campin, Portrait of a Stout Man. Robert de Masmines (?), ca. 1425, oil on panel, 35.4 × 23.7 cm, Room 5.
tracks.listen: How a picture smaller than a school notebook carries the weight of a king, and why the Henry we all picture comes from a wall that no longer exists.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 5 · Extra · Hans Memling — Portrait of a Young Man praying
tracks.where: Room 5, "15th and 16th Centuries. Renaissance Portraiture". Look for a small panel, about 29 by 22 cm: a young man in three-quarter view with his hands joined in prayer, in a loggia that opens onto a landscape, with a patterned rug on the ledge in front of him.
tracks.what: Hans Memling, Portrait of a Young Man praying (recto), ca. 1485, oil on panel, 29.2 × 22.5 cm, inv. 284.a (1938.1.a). On the reverse: Flowers in a Jug.
tracks.listen: The missing Virgin this young man was praying to, and the jug of flowers on the back that is one of the first still lifes in art.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 6 · Paris Bordone — Portrait of a Young Woman
tracks.where: Room 6, "16th Century. Villahermosa Gallery", the long gallery that runs from Room 5 towards Room 13. Find the half-length Venetian woman, about 103 by 83 cm, in a low-cut, costly dress, holding two roses, with a small monkey on a chain eating on a ledge beside her.
tracks.what: Paris Bordone, Portrait of a Young Woman, ca. 1543–1550, oil on canvas, 103 × 83 cm, inv. 55 (1936.5). Also: Pier Francesco Mola, Saint John the Baptist Preaching in the Desert, ca. 1650–1655, oil on canvas, 73.5 × 99 cm, Room 6. The building: Palacio de Villahermosa.
tracks.listen: The palace you are walking through, and a Venetian beauty who keeps temptation on a very short chain.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 7 · Vittore Carpaccio — Young Knight in a Landscape
tracks.where: Room 7, "16th Century. Italian Painting", one of the rooms off the long side of Room 6. Find the tall canvas, over two metres high: a young man in armour standing full length in a meadow thick with plants and flowers, a deer by a lake, a rider in the background and a small weasel near a scroll with writing.
tracks.what: Vittore Carpaccio, Young Knight in a Landscape, ca. 1505 (cartellino dated M.D.X.), oil on canvas, 218.5 × 151.5 cm, inv. 82 (1935.3).
tracks.listen: How a saint turned into a knight, why he may be the first full-length portrait we know, and the motto that says better to die than be defiled.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 7 · Extra · Titian — Portrait of Doge Francesco Venier
tracks.where: Room 7, "16th Century. Italian Painting". Look for an old man in the doge's gold brocade robes and cap, about 113 by 99 cm, standing before a curtain, with a window on the left where a boat is burning on the water.
tracks.what: Titian (Tiziano Vecellio), Portrait of Doge Francesco Venier, ca. 1554–1556, oil on canvas, 113 × 99 cm, inv. 405 (1930.116).
tracks.listen: The official portrait that burned with the Doge's Palace, the replica Titian made himself, and a frail ruler with a sharp eye.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 9 · Lucas Cranach the Elder — Portrait of the Emperor Charles V
tracks.where: Room 9, "15th and 16th Centuries. German Painting", after Room 8. Find the half-length portrait, about 51 by 36 cm, of a man turned to the left, with a long face, a jutting jaw and a gold chain with a small golden fleece hanging from it.
tracks.what: Lucas Cranach the Elder, Portrait of the Emperor Charles V, 1533, oil on panel, 51.2 × 36 cm, inv. 112 (1933.7). Also: Hans Holbein the Elder, Portrait of a Woman, ca. 1518–1520, oil on panel, 23.6 × 17 cm, Room 9; Albrecht Altdorfer, Portrait of a young Woman, ca. 1522, oil on panel, 59 × 45 cm, Room 9; passed in Room 8: Lucas Cranach the Elder, The Virgin and Child with a Bunch of Grapes, ca. 1509–1510, oil on panel.
tracks.listen: Spain's emperor painted by the great painter of the Reformation, and two women who have been given the wrong names.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Renaissance portraits and the Villahermosa Gallery
tracks.title: Room 10 · Joachim Patinir — Landscape with the Rest on the Flight into Egypt
tracks.where: Room 10, "16th Century. Netherlandish Painting". Find the small horizontal panel, about 32 by 58 cm, seen from high up: the Virgin and Child resting by a fountain in front, Joseph in the trees behind them, a river winding away on the left and a fortress on a rocky hill on the right.
tracks.what: Joachim Patinir, Landscape with the Rest on the Flight into Egypt, ca. 1518–1524, oil on panel, 31.5 × 57.5 cm, inv. 314 (1930.85). Also: Jan Wellens de Cock, The Temptation of Saint Anthony, ca. 1520, oil on panel, 60 × 45.5 cm, Room 10; Jan Mostaert, The Expulsion of Hagar, ca. 1520–1525, oil on panel, 94 × 131 cm, Room 10.
tracks.listen: The painter Dürer called a good landscape painter, a holy family that has become small, and a saint who has to pray very hard.

tracks.title: Room 11 · El Greco — The Annunciation
tracks.where: Room 11, "Tiziano, Tintoretto, Bassano and El Greco". Find the canvas about 117 by 98 cm: the Virgin at a prayer desk on the left, the angel arriving on the right, a chequered floor, a pink curtain and angels in a cloud of light above.
tracks.what: El Greco (Domenikos Theotokopoulos), The Annunciation, ca. 1576, oil on canvas, 117 × 98 cm, inv. 172 (1975.35). Also: Tintoretto, The Meeting of Tamar and Judah, and The Annunciation to Manoah's Wife, both ca. 1555–1559, oil on canvas, 150 × 155 cm, Room 11.
tracks.listen: Venice's lesson in colour, and El Greco before Toledo, borrowing from three great Venetians at once.

tracks.title: Room 11 · Extra · Titian — The Penitent Saint Jerome
tracks.where: Room 11, "Tiziano, Tintoretto, Bassano and El Greco". Look for a dark night scene, about 137 by 97 cm: an old, half-naked saint kneeling among rocks in a red tunic, a stone in his hand, a crucifix on a branch and a lion in the lower right corner.
tracks.what: Titian (Tiziano Vecellio), The Penitent Saint Jerome, ca. 1575, oil on canvas, 137 × 97 cm, inv. 406 (1933.4).
tracks.listen: The hidden moon, the one splash of red, and what Titian left out in his last years.

tracks.title: Room 12 · Caravaggio — Saint Catherine of Alexandria
tracks.where: Room 12, "17th Century. Caravaggio and Baroque Painting". Find the large dark canvas, about 173 by 133 cm: a young woman in a rich blue-violet dress kneeling on a red cushion, leaning on a broken spiked wheel, a sword across her lap, light falling on her from the right.
tracks.what: Caravaggio (Michelangelo Merisi), Saint Catherine of Alexandria, ca. 1598–99, oil on canvas, 173 × 133 cm, inv. 81 (1934.37). Also: Jose de Ribera, The Pietà, 1633, oil on canvas, 157 × 210 cm, Room 12.
tracks.listen: A celebrated Roman courtesan posed as a royal martyr, the cardinal who commissioned her, and why the light comes from the wrong side.

tracks.title: Room 14 · Luca Giordano — The Judgement of Solomon
tracks.where: Room 14, "17th Century. Italian, French and Spanish Painting", beside Room 13. Find the huge canvas, about 2.5 by 3 metres: King Solomon on his throne with his arm stretched out, two women below, and a baby held upside down by one ankle at the top of a pyramid of figures.
tracks.what: Luca Giordano, The Judgement of Solomon (El juicio de Salomón), ca. 1665, oil on canvas, 250.8 × 308 cm, inv. CTB.1991.8, Carmen Thyssen Collection. Also: Bernardo Cavallino, Lot and his Daughters, ca. 1640–1645, oil on panel, 41 × 38 cm, CTB.1994.3.1, Carmen Thyssen Collection, Room 14.
tracks.listen: The Bible's most famous test of motherhood, a young Neapolitan painter at full stretch, and the painter's later years at the court of King Charles II in Madrid.

tracks.title: Room 15 · Francisco de Zurbarán — Christ on the Cross
tracks.where: Room 15, "17th Century. Italian, French and Spanish Painting". Stand before the tall canvas, over two metres high, of Christ alone on the cross, pale and strongly lit against a black background. The large, soft-coloured Murillo altarpiece with a young saint and the Virgin and Child is in the same room.
tracks.what: Francisco de Zurbarán, Christ on the Cross, ca. 1630, oil on canvas, 214 × 143.5 cm, inv. 447. Also: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Virgin and Child with Saint Rose of Viterbo, ca. 1670, oil on canvas, 190 × 147 cm, inv. 296.
tracks.listen: Why Zurbarán paints Christ still alive, the four nails of the Seville tradition, and Murillo's softer way of praying forty years later.

tracks.title: Room 16 · Giambattista Piazzetta — Portrait of a Young Woman in Profile with a Mask in her Right Hand
tracks.where: Room 16, "18th Century. Italian Painting". Look for a small canvas, under half a metre high, of a young woman turning her head in profile, a black cloak over her shoulders and a tiny mask held between finger and thumb. Longhi's small interior with a girl tickling a sleeping man, and Tiepolo's small oil sketch of a dying queen, are in the same room.
tracks.what: Giambattista Piazzetta, Portrait of a Young Woman in Profile with a Mask in her Right Hand (Retrato de una joven de perfil con una máscara en la mano derecha), ca. 1720–1730, oil on canvas, 46 × 36.2 cm, Carmen Thyssen Collection, CTB.1999.5. Also: Pietro Longhi, The Tickle, ca. 1755, oil on canvas, inv. 224; Giambattista Tiepolo, The Death of Sophonisba, ca. 1760, oil on canvas, inv. 396.
tracks.listen: An introduction to 18th-century Venice through a woman caught mid-Carnival, the painter's future wife perhaps, with Longhi's comedy and Tiepolo's tragedy alongside.

tracks.title: Room 17 · Canaletto — The Grand Canal from San Vio, Venice
tracks.where: Room 17, "18th Century. Italian Painting". Stand before the two large, bright Canalettos hung as a pair, each about two metres wide: the Grand Canal under a big blue sky, and the Piazza San Marco seen from high up. The two small, misty Guardi views of the Grand Canal are in the same room.
tracks.what: Canaletto (Giovanni Antonio Canal), The Grand Canal from San Vio, Venice, ca. 1723–1724, oil on canvas, 140.5 × 204.5 cm, inv. 76. Also: Canaletto, The Piazza San Marco in Venice, ca. 1723–1724, oil on canvas, 141.5 × 204.5 cm, inv. 75; Francesco Guardi, The Grand Canal with Santa Lucia and Santa Maria di Nazareth and The Grand Canal with San Simeone Piccolo and Santa Lucia, both ca. 1780, oil on canvas, 48 × 78 cm, inv. 174 and 175.
tracks.listen: How the paving of St Mark's Square dates Canaletto's early pair, and how Guardi painted the same city half a century later as light and air.

tracks.title: Room 17 · Extra · Giambattista Tiepolo — The Death of Hyacinthus
tracks.where: Room 17. Find the huge canvas, nearly three metres high, of a youth lying on the ground and an anguished Apollo bending over him, with a tennis racquet and balls on the tiled floor.
tracks.what: Giambattista Tiepolo, The Death of Hyacinthus, ca. 1752–1753, oil on canvas, 287 × 232 cm, inv. 394. Cue only: Giambattista Piazzetta, Portrait of Giulia Lama, ca. 1715–1720, oil on canvas, inv. 316, Room 18.
tracks.listen: Why Tiepolo turned Ovid's fatal discus into a game of tennis, and the smiling statue that watches it all.

tracks.title: Room 22 · Extra · Giuseppe Maria Crespi — Portrait of Count Fulvio Grati, and two peasant scenes on copper
tracks.where: Room 22, "18th Century. Italian Painting". Stand before the tall, almost life-size portrait of a seated nobleman with a lute on his lap, a curtain behind him and a Black page at the right. The two small paintings on copper of peasant life are by the same painter, in the same room.
tracks.what: Giuseppe Maria Crespi, Portrait of Count Fulvio Grati, ca. 1720–1723, oil on canvas, 228 × 153 cm, inv. 116. Also: Crespi, Peasants with Donkeys (Campesinos con asnos) and Interior with a Family of Peasants (Interior con familia de campesinos), both ca. 1709, oil on copper, 39.4 × 31.1 cm, Carmen Thyssen Collection, CTB.1994.1.2 and CTB.1994.1.1.
tracks.listen: One Bolognese painter at both ends of society: a count dressed for music, and peasants painted without mockery.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 23 · Frans Hals — Family Group in a Landscape
tracks.where: Room 23, "17th Century. Dutch Painting. Landscape". Stand before the huge canvas, about two metres high and almost three wide, of a family posed outdoors, husband and wife holding hands, a dog beside a little girl, and a wide landscape opening on the right. Van Goyen's small frozen river scene is in the same room.
tracks.what: Frans Hals, Family Group in a Landscape (Grupo familiar ante un paisaje), 1645–1648, oil on canvas, 202 × 285 cm, inv. 179. Also: Jan Josephsz. van Goyen, Winter Landscape with Figures on Ice (Paisaje invernal con figuras en el hielo), 1643, oil on panel, inv. 167.
tracks.listen: An introduction to the Dutch rooms through a family portrait in a landscape room, and the second painter who may have painted its view.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 24 · Jean-Honoré Fragonard — The See-Saw
tracks.where: Room 24, the long gallery of "18th Century. French and English Painting". Look for an upright canvas, just over a metre high, of children playing in a leafy wood, with a girl flying up on a see-saw. Boucher's small, cluttered boudoir scene and Gainsborough's young woman in pale blue in a garden are in the same gallery.
tracks.what: Jean-Honoré Fragonard, The See-Saw (El columpio), ca. 1750–1752, oil on canvas, 120 × 94.5 cm, inv. 148. Also: François Boucher, La Toilette, 1742, oil on canvas, inv. 58; Thomas Gainsborough, Portrait of Sarah Buxton, ca. 1776–1777, oil on canvas, 110 × 87 cm, inv. 153.
tracks.listen: The young Fragonard's game in the woods and the Paris collector who links it to his famous Swing, with Boucher's boudoir and a Gainsborough rescued from a fire.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 24 · Louise Moillon — Still-Life with Fruit
tracks.where: Room 24, the long gallery of 18th-century French and English painting. Look for a wide still life, about a metre across, of spring fruit and vegetables on a table under a canopy of leaves: a Chinese bowl of strawberries on the left, artichokes and asparagus behind, a basket of apricots on a dish propped on two bricks at the right.
tracks.what: Louise Moillon, Still-Life with Fruit (Bodegón con frutas), ca. 1637, oil on canvas, 87.5 × 112 cm, Carmen Thyssen Collection, CTB.1956.12.
tracks.listen: A Paris still-life painter at the height of her powers, and how this picture marks the change in her style.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 24 · Extra · Jean Antoine Watteau — Pierrot Content
tracks.where: Room 24. Look for one of the smallest pictures in the gallery, about 35 centimetres high: a garden corner under dark trees, with Pierrot in white sitting between two women and two men, one woman playing a guitar.
tracks.what: Jean Antoine Watteau, Pierrot Content (Pierrot contento), ca. 1712, oil on canvas, 35 × 31 cm, inv. 432.
tracks.listen: Watteau's little scene from the Italian comedy, the figures that have faded into the trees, and its afterlife in Lucian Freud's portrait of Baron Thyssen.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 25 · Nicolaes Maes — The Naughty Drummer
tracks.where: Room 25, "17th Century. Dutch Painting. Scenes of Daily Life and Interiors". Look for a small, almost square interior, about 60 centimetres across: a mother by the window with sewing on her lap, raising a little rod at a boy with a drum, a baby asleep in a wicker cradle. Kalf's still life with a Chinese bowl and a nautilus cup, and Steen's self-portrait with a lute, are in the same room.
tracks.what: Nicolaes Maes, The Naughty Drummer (El tamborilero desobediente), ca. 1655, oil on canvas, 62 × 66.4 cm, inv. 241. Also: Willem Kalf, Still Life with a Chinese Bowl, Nautilus Cup and Other Objects, 1662, oil on canvas, inv. 203; Jan Havicksz. Steen, Self-Portrait playing the Lute, ca. 1663–1665, oil on panel, inv. 373.
tracks.listen: A mother, a drum and a sleeping baby, the man in the mirror, and three ways of reading one Dutch interior.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 26 · Pieter Jansz. Saenredam — The West Façade of the Church of Saint Mary in Utrecht
tracks.where: Room 26, "17th Century. Dutch Painting. Landscape". Look for a pale, upright panel, about 65 centimetres high, of a plain Romanesque church front among trees, with three tiny figures at its foot. Cuyp's golden sunset with a cowherd and a wooden bridge is in the same room.
tracks.what: Pieter Jansz. Saenredam, The West Façade of the Church of Saint Mary in Utrecht, 1662, oil on panel, 65.1 × 51.2 cm, inv. 362. Also: Aelbert Jacobsz. Cuyp, Landscape with a Sunset, ca. 1655, oil on panel, 48.3 × 74.9 cm, inv. 117.
tracks.listen: How Saenredam measured a church in 1636, painted it a quarter of a century later, and quietly improved it.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 27 · Rembrandt — Self-portrait wearing a hat and two Chains
tracks.where: Room 27, "17th Century. Dutch Painting. Portrait". Look for a dark panel, about 70 centimetres high, of a man almost face on in a dark hat and dark clothes, with a white shirt and two gold chains as the only bright notes. De Keyser's small portrait of two women and a boy with a watch is in the same room.
tracks.what: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn, Self-portrait wearing a hat and two Chains (Autorretrato con gorra y dos cadenas), ca. 1642–1643, oil on panel, 72 × 54.8 cm, inv. 331. Also: Thomas Hendricksz. de Keyser, Portrait of Two Women and a Boy, 1632, oil on panel, 70.2 × 50.2 cm, inv. 209.
tracks.listen: How a doubted self-portrait was confirmed as Rembrandt's own, partly by the wood it is painted on, and the chains he was never given.

tracks.section: Level 2 · The Dutch Golden Age and the French salon
tracks.title: Room 28 · Jacob van Ruisdael — View of Naarden, and Stormy Sea with Sailing Vessels
tracks.where: Room 28, "17th Century. Dutch Painting. Landscape". Start with the small, wide panel, under 70 centimetres across, of flat fields and a distant town under a sky of cloud bands. The stormy sea, with a narrow strip of grey water under a towering sky, and the view of a road through ripe wheat are by the same painter, in the same room.
tracks.what: Jacob Isaacksz. van Ruisdael, View of Naarden, 1647, oil on panel, 34.8 × 67 cm, inv. 354; Stormy Sea with Sailing Vessels (Mar tormentoso con barcos de vela), ca. 1668, oil on canvas, 50.1 × 62.5 cm, inv. 359. Also: Road trough Grain Fields near the Zuider Zee (official title spelling), ca. 1660–1662, oil on canvas, inv. 357.
tracks.listen: Ruisdael's career in one room, from the teenager's view of his family's town to a sea under three-quarters sky, and the Turner who may have seen it.

tracks.title: Room 29 · Caspar David Friedrich — Easter Morning
tracks.where: Room 29, "19th Century. European Painting. Goya and Romanticism". Look for a small upright canvas, under half a metre high, of three women on a steep, winding path at dawn, with snow on the ground, old trees and a pale moon high in the sky. Delacroix's two small paintings are in the same room.
tracks.what: Caspar David Friedrich, Easter Morning (Mañana de Pascua), ca. 1828–1835, oil on canvas, 43.7 × 34.4 cm, inv. 792.
tracks.listen: The start of the 19th century, and how Friedrich paints the Resurrection with nothing but a path, a moon and the first green shoots.

tracks.title: Room 29 · Extra · Eugène Delacroix — Arab Rider
tracks.where: Room 29. Look for a small upright panel, about 35 centimetres high, of a man resting on the ground by a fire with a restless black horse standing behind him. Delacroix's other small painting here shows a duke lifting a sheet beside a curtained bed.
tracks.what: Eugène Delacroix, Arab Rider (Jinete árabe), ca. 1854, oil on panel, 35 × 26.5 cm, inv. 126. Also: Delacroix, The Duke of Orleans showing his Lover, ca. 1825–1826, oil on canvas, 35 × 25.5 cm, inv. 127.
tracks.listen: A memory of Delacroix's 1832 journey to Morocco, noted in his diary more than twenty years later, and a much earlier, scandalous tale beside it.

tracks.title: Room 30 · Circle of Sir Joshua Reynolds (?) — Portrait of a Man from the Island of Dominica (?)
tracks.where: Room 30, "18th and 19th Century. Transatlantic relations", beside the lift and stairs. Look for a bust portrait, under a metre high, of a Black man in white, wearing an unusual hat, set in a painted oval. Copley's portrait of a Boston merchant's wife in pink, with pearls and a blue shawl, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Circle of Sir Joshua Reynolds (?), Portrait of a Man from the Island of Dominica (?), ca. 1770–1780, oil on canvas, 76 × 63.5 cm, inv. 383. Also: John Singleton Copley, Portrait of Mrs. Joshua Henshaw II (Catherine Hill), ca. 1772, oil on canvas, 77 × 56 cm, inv. 97.
tracks.listen: An introduction to Level 1 and Baron Hans Heinrich's American collection, through a portrait whose sitter, painter and hat are still a mystery.

tracks.title: Room 31 · Frederic Edwin Church — Cross in the Wilderness
tracks.where: Room 31, "19th Century. American Landscape and Environmental Awareness". Look for a small, wide canvas, about 60 centimetres across, of a lone cross hung with garlands in a rocky landscape, a waterfall and lake to its right, under a vast evening sky. Thomas Cole's larger, darker scene of a stone bridge and glowing arch over an abyss is in the same room.
tracks.what: Frederic Edwin Church, Cross in the Wilderness, 1857, oil on canvas, 41.3 × 61.5 cm, inv. 508. Also: Thomas Cole, Expulsion. Moon and Firelight (Expulsión. Luna y luz de fuego), ca. 1828, oil on canvas, 91.4 × 122 cm, inv. 95.
tracks.listen: A landscape painted in memory of a dead child, the Andean roadside crosses behind it, and the teacher who saw America as an Eden at risk.

tracks.title: Room 32 · John Singer Sargent — Portrait of Millicent, Duchess of Sutherland
tracks.where: Room 32, "19th Century. American Landscape and Urban Life". Stand before the tall full-length portrait, two and a half metres high, of a red-haired woman in a flowered green dress in a shaded garden, one hand on a fountain. Harnett's small trompe-l'oeil table with a pipe and a newspaper is in the same room.
tracks.what: John Singer Sargent, Portrait of Millicent, Duchess of Sutherland, 1904, oil on canvas, 254 × 146 cm, inv. 732. Also: William Michael Harnett, Materials for a Leisure Hour (Objetos para un rato de ocio), 1879, oil on canvas, 38 × 51.5 cm, inv. 574.
tracks.listen: The duchess who was a hostess, writer, charity worker and wartime nurse, the critics who argued over her portrait, and Harnett's pipe that is still smoking.

tracks.title: Room 33 · Berthe Morisot — The Psyche mirror
tracks.where: Room 33, "The Impressionist Period". Stand in front of the medium-sized canvas of a young woman in a white dressing gown, standing in her bedroom before a tall, tilting mirror on a stand.
tracks.what: Berthe Morisot, The Psyche mirror (El espejo psiqué), 1876, oil on canvas, 65 × 54 cm. Also: Édouard Manet, Horsewoman, Full-Face (L'Amazone), about 1882, oil on canvas, and Edgar Degas, Swaying Dancer (Dancer in Green), 1877–1879, pastel and gouache on paper, both in Room 33.
tracks.listen: How a sneering review named a movement, and how one of its founders painted a private room with her own mirror in it.

tracks.title: Room 33 · Extra · Camille Pissarro — Rue Saint-Honoré in the Afternoon. Effect of Rain
tracks.where: Room 33, "The Impressionist Period". Look for the upright canvas of a long Paris street seen from high above just after rain, with horse-drawn carriages, a few umbrellas and the corner of a square in the foreground.
tracks.what: Camille Pissarro, Rue Saint-Honoré in the Afternoon. Effect of Rain, 1897, oil on canvas, 81 × 65 cm.
tracks.listen: A country painter in a hotel room, painting every view from his window through one Paris winter.

tracks.title: Room 34 · Vincent van Gogh — The Stevedores in Arles
tracks.where: Room 34, "Expressionist Landscapes". Find the small horizontal canvas of dark boats and tiny figures against a blazing orange sunset over a river.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, The Stevedores in Arles, 1888, oil on canvas, 54 × 65 cm. Also: André Derain, Waterloo Bridge, 1906, oil on canvas, Room 34.
tracks.listen: How the Baron's modern collecting began, and the evening on the Rhône that Van Gogh called "pure Hokusai".

tracks.title: Room 35 · Gabriele Münter — Self-portrait
tracks.where: Room 35, "Expressionist Portraits". Find the small upright picture on cardboard of a woman with a serious, inward look, her face built of thick brushstrokes and the rest barely sketched.
tracks.what: Gabriele Münter, Self-portrait, about 1909–1910, oil on cardboard, 49 × 33.6 cm. Also: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Fränzi in front of Carved Chair, 1910, oil on canvas, and Doris with Ruff Collar, about 1906, oil on cardboard, both Room 35.
tracks.listen: A self-portrait its painter never showed anyone, and the two Kirchners that started the Baron's modern collection.

tracks.title: Room 36 · Extra · James Ensor — Theatre of Masks
tracks.where: Room 36, "The Language of the Body". Look for the horizontal painting of a brightly lit stage crowded with grotesque masked faces, in a gilt frame shaped like a little theatre.
tracks.what: James Ensor, Theatre of Masks, 1908, oil on canvas, 72 × 86 cm. Also: Mikhail Larionov, Blue Nude, about 1908, oil on canvas, Room 36.
tracks.listen: A boy who grew up among carnival masks, and the crowd that turns into one.

tracks.title: Room 37 · George Grosz — Metropolis
tracks.where: Room 37, "Urban unrest". Stand in front of the square canvas that burns red from edge to edge: a crowded city street under a blazing, unreal sun.
tracks.what: George Grosz, Metropolis, 1916–1917, oil on canvas, 100 × 102 cm. Also: Wassily Kandinsky, Murnau: Top of the Johannisstrasse, 1908, oil on cardboard, Room 37.
tracks.listen: A city painted in the colour of fire in the middle of the First World War, and the long road the canvas travelled afterwards.

tracks.title: Room 38 · Extra · Henri Matisse — The Yellow Flowers
tracks.where: Room 38, "Flowers", a small room. Look for the modest horizontal still life in muted tones: a vase of yellow flowers, with its reflection glowing in a mirror behind it.
tracks.what: Henri Matisse, The Yellow Flowers (Las flores amarillas), 1902, oil on canvas, 46 × 54.5 cm. Also: Max Beckmann, Still life with Yellow Roses, 1937, oil on canvas, Room 38.
tracks.listen: Two flower paintings made in hard times: one by a painter close to ruin, one by a painter in exile.

tracks.title: Room 39 · Wassily Kandinsky — In the Bright Oval
tracks.where: Room 39, "Pioneers of abstraction". Stand in front of the upright painting on cardboard with a large bright oval and geometric shapes, lines and points of colour.
tracks.what: Wassily Kandinsky, In the Bright Oval (En el óvalo claro), 1925, oil on cardboard, 73 × 59 cm. Also: František Kupka, Localization of Graphic Mobiles I, 1912–1913, oil on canvas, 200 × 194 cm, Room 39.
tracks.listen: How the painter of the Murnau street ended up teaching that a triangle has a colour, and why this is more than geometry.

tracks.title: Room 40 · Marc Chagall — The Madonna of the Village
tracks.where: Room 40, "Popular flavor". Stand in front of the large, nearly square canvas of a huge Madonna in a white bridal gown holding the Child, floating among angels, with a flying cow playing the violin.
tracks.what: Marc Chagall, The Madonna of the Village (La Virgen de la aldea), 1938–1942, oil on canvas, 102.5 × 98 cm. Also: Marc Chagall, The Grey House, 1917, oil on canvas, Room 40.
tracks.listen: A painting that travelled with Chagall as he fled the Nazis, and a hometown picture with a joke written on its fence.

tracks.title: Room 41 · Pablo Picasso — Man with a Clarinet, and Georges Braque — Woman with a Mandolin
tracks.where: Room 41, "The Cubist Tradition I". Find the two upright Cubist canvases in browns, ochres and greys: Picasso's pyramid-shaped figure built of splintered planes, and Braque's slightly smaller seated woman whose mandolin and hand you can just make out.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Man with a Clarinet, 1911–1912, oil on canvas, 106 × 69 cm; Georges Braque, Woman with a Mandolin (Mujer con mandolina), 1910, oil on canvas, 80.5 × 54 cm. Also: Paul Cézanne, Seated Man, 1905–1906, and Juan Gris, The Smoker (Frank Haviland), 1913, both oil on canvas, Room 41.
tracks.listen: Where Cubism came from, how to find a figure in it, and why three of these paintings went under the hammer in 1921.

tracks.title: Room 42 · Sonia Delaunay — Simultaneous Contrasts
tracks.where: Room 42, "The Cubist Tradition II". Find the small horizontal canvas made only of curved bands and segments of clashing colour, reds against blues. Robert Delaunay's taller Woman with a Parasol hangs in the same room.
tracks.what: Sonia Delaunay, Simultaneous Contrasts (Contrastes simultáneos), 1913, oil on canvas, 46 × 55 cm. Also: Robert Delaunay, Woman with a Parasol, 1913, oil on canvas, 121 × 85 cm, and Giacomo Balla, Patriotic Demonstration, 1915, oil on canvas, Room 42.
tracks.listen: A picture that was probably hung the wrong way up, and why a painter who had been designing bedspreads would not have minded.

tracks.title: Room 43 · Liubov Popova — Painterly Architectonic, and Olga Rozanova — Man on the Street (Analysis of Volumes)
tracks.where: Room 43, "Abstract Utopias". Find Popova's small horizontal canvas of overlapping coloured planes, and nearby Rozanova's taller canvas of a figure in the street analysed into geometric volumes.
tracks.what: Liubov Popova, Painterly Architectonic (Arquitectura pictórica), 1918, oil on canvas, 45 × 53 cm; Olga Rozanova, Man on the Street (Analysis of Volumes), 1913, oil on canvas, 83 × 61.5 cm. Also: El Lissitzky, Proun 1 C, 1919, oil on panel, Room 43.
tracks.listen: Two Russian women at the heart of the avant-garde, and a painting that wanted to become a building.

tracks.title: Room 43 · Extra · Piet Mondrian — New York City, 3 (unfinished)
tracks.where: Room 43, "Abstract Utopias". Look for the nearly square canvas crossed by thin coloured lines, made of strips of adhesive tape rather than paint.
tracks.what: Piet Mondrian, New York City, 3 (unfinished), 1941, oil, pencil, chalk and coloured tape on canvas, 117 × 110 cm. Also: Piet Mondrian, Composition No. XIII/ Composition 2, 1913, oil on canvas, Room 43.
tracks.listen: Why the lines in this Mondrian are made of tape, and what New York did to a painter who had spent his life in Europe.

tracks.title: Room 44 · René Magritte — The Key of the Fields (La Clef des champs)
tracks.where: Room 44, "Dada and Surrealism". Stand in front of the upright canvas of a window smashed open onto a landscape, with shards of glass on the floor that still carry pieces of the view.
tracks.what: René Magritte, The Key of the Fields (La Clef des champs), 1936, oil on canvas, 80 × 60 cm. Also: Kurt Schwitters, Merzbild Kijkduin, 1923, oil, pencil and wood assemblage on cardboard, Room 44.
tracks.listen: What Dada and Surrealism wanted, and a broken window that makes you doubt what you just saw.

tracks.title: Room 45 · Edward Hopper — Hotel Room
tracks.where: Room 45, "Interwar Realisms". Stand in front of the big, almost square canvas, about one and a half metres across, of a woman in her slip sitting on the edge of a hotel bed under hard light, reading a yellowed sheet of paper.
tracks.what: Edward Hopper, Hotel Room (Habitación de hotel), 1931, oil on canvas, 152.4 × 165.7 cm. Also: Otto Dix, Hugo Erfurth with Dog, 1926, tempera and oil on panel, and Pablo Picasso, Harlequin with a Mirror, 1923, oil on canvas, both Room 45.
tracks.listen: The night before a train, a wife who posed and kept the notes, and two other portraits that hide as much as they show.

tracks.title: Room 45 · Extra · Balthus — The Card Game
tracks.where: Room 45, "Interwar Realisms". Look for the wide canvas, almost two metres across, of a boy and a girl playing cards at a table with a candlestick, in a bare, stark room lit from the right.
tracks.what: Balthus (Balthazar Klossowski de Rola), The Card Game, 1948–1950, oil on canvas, 140 × 194 cm. Also: Max Beckmann, Quappi in Pink Jumper, 1932–1934, oil on canvas, Room 45.
tracks.listen: A card game in which the girl always wins, and a portrait whose smile was turned down as the Nazis came to power.

tracks.title: Room 46 · Jackson Pollock — Brown and Silver I
tracks.where: Room 46, "American Abstraction I". Stand in front of the canvas, about one and a half metres by one, of dark brown lines and shapes on raw canvas, splashed with patches of silver paint.
tracks.what: Jackson Pollock, Brown and Silver I, about 1951, enamel and silver paint on canvas, 144.7 × 107.9 cm. Also: Arshile Gorky, Last Painting, 1948, oil on canvas, Room 46.
tracks.listen: How New York took over from Paris, and why Pollock's famous drips gave way to dark, half-figurative lines.

tracks.title: Room 46 · Georgia O'Keeffe — White Iris No. 7
tracks.where: In Room 46, "American Abstraction I", the same room as the Pollock. White Iris No. 7 is an upright canvas about a metre high, one pale flower so close that its petals run off every edge. From the Plains II is the wide canvas nearly two metres across, in bands of flaming red, orange and yellow.
tracks.what: Georgia O'Keeffe, White Iris No. 7 (Lirio blanco nº 7), 1957, oil on canvas, 102 × 76.2 cm, inv. 697. Also: Georgia O'Keeffe, From the Plains II (Desde las llanuras II), 1954, oil on canvas, 122 × 183 cm, inv. 696. Both Room 46, Level 1.
tracks.listen: Why O'Keeffe pushed her eye right into a flower, why she rejected what people saw there, and how a memory of Texas cattle became pure colour.

tracks.title: Room 47 · Mark Rothko — Untitled (Green on Maroon)
tracks.where: In Room 47, "American Abstraction II", the small room between 46 and 48. The Rothko is the biggest canvas here, taller than a person: a dark field of green floating on maroon, as the title says. Stand about an arm's length or two away.
tracks.what: Mark Rothko, Untitled (Green on Maroon) (ES: Sin título, Verde sobre morado), 1961, mixed media on canvas, 258 × 229 cm, inv. 729, Room 47, Level 1. English title used, as PLAN directs.
tracks.listen: Why Rothko wanted his huge paintings seen close up, how his colour darkened in 1961, and the thread back to Friedrich upstairs.

tracks.title: Room 48 · Romare Bearden — Sunday After Sermon
tracks.where: In Room 48, "Post-war American Art", the corner room at the end of this wing. Sunday After Sermon is a collage about a metre high and a little wider, a street full of figures cut from magazines and newspapers. Express is the long canvas, three metres wide, crowded with grainy printed photographs.
tracks.what: Romare Bearden, Sunday After Sermon (Domingo después del sermón), 1969, collage on cardboard, 101.6 × 127 cm, inv. 462, Room 48, Level 1. Also: Robert Rauschenberg, Express, 1963, oil and silkscreen ink on canvas, 184.2 × 305.2 cm, inv. 721; Joseph Cornell, Juan Gris Cockatoo No. 4, ca. 1953–1954, construction and collage, inv. 491. All Room 48.
tracks.listen: A Harlem studio meeting in the year of the march on Washington, a street scene cut from magazines, and how Rauschenberg printed the news onto canvas.

tracks.title: Room 49 · Lucian Freud — Portrait of a Man (Baron H.H. Thyssen-Bornemisza)
tracks.where: In Room 49, "Post-war European Figurative Art". The Baron's portrait is small, about half a metre high: a man in a checked jacket, white shirt and dark tie, head tipped forward, eyes lowered. Reflection with Two Children is the square canvas nearby, Freud seen from below with two tiny children in the lower corner.
tracks.what: Lucian Freud, Portrait of a Man (Baron H.H. Thyssen-Bornemisza), 1981–1982, oil on canvas, 51 × 40 cm, inv. 551, Room 49, Level 1. Also: Lucian Freud, Reflection with Two Children (Self-Portrait), 1965, oil on canvas, 91 × 91 cm, inv. 550, Room 49.
tracks.listen: The collector who had never sat for a portrait, nearly two years in Freud's studio, and the Watteau hidden over his shoulder.

tracks.title: Room 50 · Extra · Frank Auerbach — Head of J.Y.M.
tracks.where: In Room 50, "Informalisms". Head of J.Y.M. is a small, almost square canvas, about sixty centimetres across, where a head emerges from thick ridges of paint. Wild Horses by Karel Appel is the tall canvas in loud primary colours.
tracks.what: Frank Auerbach, Head of J.Y.M. (Cabeza de J. Y. M.), 1978, oil on canvas, 61 × 66 cm, inv. 455, Room 50, Level 1. Also: Karel Appel, Wild Horses, 1954, oil on canvas, 194.5 × 113 cm, inv. 454, Room 50.
tracks.listen: A portrait made almost entirely of paint, of a model whose name hides behind three initials.

tracks.title: Room 51 · Extra · Richard Estes — Telephone Booths
tracks.where: In Room 51, "Homo Ludens". Telephone Booths is the wide picture, nearly two metres across, of a row of glass and metal phone booths on a New York corner, each with a person inside, back turned. People's Flowers is the tall upright canvas by the same artist, a shopfront with a neon sign at its centre.
tracks.what: Richard Estes, Telephone Booths, 1967, acrylic on masonite, 122 × 175.3 cm, inv. 539, Room 51, Level 1. Also: Richard Estes, People's Flowers, 1971, oil on canvas, 153 × 101.2 cm, CTB.1975.24 (Carmen Thyssen Collection), Room 51.
tracks.listen: How Estes built one street corner out of several photographs, and why the glass will not let your eye settle.

tracks.title: Room 52 · Roy Lichtenstein — Woman in Bath, and David Hockney — In Memoriam of Cecchino Bracci
tracks.where: In Room 52, "Pop Art", the last room on this floor. Woman in Bath is the big square canvas, about 1.7 metres each way, of a smiling comic-strip woman against a tiled wall, in red, yellow and blue dots. Hockney's In Memoriam of Cecchino Bracci is the tall, narrow canvas, over two metres high, shaped like a tomb.
tracks.what: Roy Lichtenstein, Woman in Bath, 1963, oil and Magna on canvas, 173.3 × 173.3 cm, inv. 648, Room 52, Level 1. David Hockney, In Memoriam of Cecchino Bracci, 1962, oil on canvas, 213.3 × 91.4 cm, inv. 584, Room 52, Level 1.
tracks.listen: How Pop painted the comics by hand, and how a young Hockney turned a Renaissance epitaph into a joke and a lament.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room A · Jan Brueghel the Elder — The Garden of Eden
tracks.where: In Room A, "Old Masters", the first room of the Carmen Thyssen collection. The Garden of Eden is a small panel, about a metre wide, packed with animals: look for a horse, a lion and lioness on the left, and two tiny figures far in the background.
tracks.what: Jan Brueghel the Elder, The Garden of Eden, ca. 1610–1612, oil on panel, 59.4 × 95.6 cm, CTB.1988.29, Carmen Thyssen Collection, Room A, Level 0. Collection intro: Carmen Thyssen collection, ground floor.
tracks.listen: Whose collection this floor is, and how Brueghel filled Paradise with animals borrowed from Rubens.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room B · Extra · Albert Bierstadt — Sundown at Yosemite
tracks.where: In Room B, "North American Landscape". Sundown at Yosemite is a small oil sketch, about forty centimetres wide: a sunset breaking between the granite walls of a valley. Heade's Orchid and Hummingbird is the picture with a pink orchid in close-up and a tiny bird beside it.
tracks.what: Albert Bierstadt, Sundown at Yosemite, ca. 1863, oil on canvas, 30.5 × 40.6 cm, CTB.1980.9, Room B, Level 0. Also: Martin Johnson Heade, Orchid and Hummingbird near a Mountain Waterfall, 1902, oil on canvas, 38.2 × 51.5 cm, CTB.1979.44, Room B.
tracks.listen: A quick sunset sketch from 1863, a valley called the Garden of Eden, and an eighty-three-year-old painter's pet hummingbirds.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room C · Vincent van Gogh — Watermill at Gennep
tracks.where: In Room C, "French Naturalist Landscape". The Van Gogh is the long, dark canvas, a metre and a half wide: a wooden watermill with two wheels on a river, a farmhouse behind, and sunbeams breaking through grey cloud above. Degas's Pond in the Forest is the small, dark woodland picture nearby.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, Watermill at Gennep, 1884, oil on canvas, 85 × 151 cm, CTB.1996.32, Room C, Level 0. Also: Edgar Degas, The Pond in the Forest, ca. 1867–1868, oil on canvas, 33.5 × 41.2 cm, CTB.2000.65, Room C.
tracks.listen: Van Gogh painting outdoors in a freezing Dutch November, the sky that melted, and why this Van Gogh hangs among the landscape painters.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room D · Berthe Morisot — Reclining Nude Shepherdess
tracks.where: In Room D, "Impressionism". Morisot's painting is the horizontal canvas, almost a metre wide, of a nude young woman lying in the open air by water, still wearing a headscarf. Sisley's Flood at Port-Marly is the smaller street scene with floodwater spreading under a big sky.
tracks.what: Berthe Morisot, Reclining Nude Shepherdess, 1891, oil on canvas, 57.5 × 86.4 cm, CTB.2000.9, Room D, Level 0. Also: Alfred Sisley, The Flood at Port-Marly, 1876, oil on canvas, 50 × 61 cm, CTB.1974.25, Room D.
tracks.listen: A summer in a rented house above the Seine, and how a founding Impressionist built her most ambitious nude the old-fashioned way.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room E · Claude Monet — The House among the Roses
tracks.where: In Room E, "Monet and North American Impressionism". The Monet is an upright canvas, nearly a metre high: the front of his house at Giverny between two big rose trees in bloom, the left one cut off by the edge of the picture. Hassam's Plaza de la Merced, Ronda is the smaller sunlit Spanish square seen from above.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, The House among the Roses, 1925, oil on canvas, 92.3 × 73.3 cm, CTB.1998.52, Room E, Level 0. Also: Childe Hassam, Plaza de la Merced, Ronda, 1910, oil on panel, 64.6 × 52 cm, CTB.1996.22, Room E.
tracks.listen: The summer Monet got his colours back after years of cataracts, and an American Impressionist who painted Andalusia without the clichés.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room F · Paul Gauguin — Mata Mua (In Olden Times)
tracks.where: In Room F, "Gauguin and Postimpressionism". Mata Mua is the upright canvas, about ninety centimetres high, in flat, glowing colour: a giant tree trunk down the middle, a woman playing a flute in front, dancers around a great stone idol, and pink and purple mountains behind. Coming and Going, Martinique is the wider landscape with women carrying baskets on their heads.
tracks.what: Paul Gauguin, Mata Mua (In Olden Times) (Mata Mua, Erase una vez), 1892, oil on canvas, 91 × 69 cm, CTB.1984.8, Room F, Level 0. Also: Paul Gauguin, Coming and Going, Martinique, 1887, oil on canvas, 72.5 × 92 cm, CTB.1979.88, Room F.
tracks.listen: The golden age Gauguin went looking for in Tahiti, the one he invented instead, and the painting's own journey out of Madrid and back.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room G · Extra · Wassily Kandinsky — The Ludwigskirche in Munich
tracks.where: In Room G, "Neo Impressionism and its Wake". The Kandinsky is a wide picture on cardboard, about a metre across: a crowd in jewel-like dabs of colour under the dark arches of a church porch. Signac's Port-en-Bessin, The Beach is the smaller, quieter seaside view.
tracks.what: Wassily Kandinsky, The Ludwigskirche in Munich, 1908, oil on cardboard, 67.3 × 96 cm, CTB.1977.101, Room G, Level 0. Also: Paul Signac, Port-en-Bessin, The Beach, 1884, oil on canvas, 46 × 64.5 cm, CTB.2000.60, Room G.
tracks.listen: A procession outside Kandinsky's front door, and how its patches of colour were already halfway to abstraction.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room H · Natalia Goncharova — Fishing (fishers)
tracks.where: In Room H, "Early Avant-gardes". Goncharova's Fishing is the almost square canvas, just over a metre high, of peasants fishing, painted in bright, flat colour with heavy outlines. Picasso's Harvesters is the smaller rural scene with a figure striding towards you, arms raised. Delaunay's Large Portuguese is the very large canvas, two metres wide, in strong, saturated colour.
tracks.what: Natalia Goncharova, Fishing (fishers), 1909, oil on canvas, 112 × 99.7 cm, CTB.1977.34, Room H, Level 0. Also: Pablo Picasso, The Harvesters (Les Moissonneurs), 1907, oil on canvas, 65 × 81.5 cm, CTB.1979.39; Robert Delaunay, Portuguese Woman (The Large Portuguese), 1916, oil and wax on canvas, 180 × 205 cm, CTB.1998.8. All Room H.
tracks.listen: The leading woman of the Russian avant-garde, who found the modern in peasant life and folk art, beside Picasso and Delaunay in the same years.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room I · Juan Gris — Seated Woman
tracks.where: In Room I, "Between the Wars Painting. Cubism, Abstraction and Surrealism". Seated Woman is the tall panel, over a metre high, of a woman in a pleated cloak and party dress, her figure built from overlapping triangles and slanting planes.
tracks.what: Juan Gris, Seated Woman (Mujer sentada), 1917, oil on panel, 116 × 73 cm, CTB.1986.23, Carmen Thyssen Collection, Room I, Level 0.
tracks.listen: A Madrid-born Cubist in wartime Paris, his partner Josette in her best dress, and the old master Gris was quietly looking at.

tracks.section: Level 0 · Carmen Thyssen collection · From Old Masters to the avant-gardes
tracks.title: Room J · Extra · Charles Bell — Thunder Smash
tracks.where: In Room J, "North American Painting and Others", the last room of the Carmen Thyssen collection. Thunder Smash is the big, glossy close-up of a pinball machine, about 1.7 metres wide, with stars, a crescent moon and comic-book explosions on a lit panel and a shining metal ball. Estes's Nedick's is the shopfront scene with a deep view into the store.
tracks.what: Charles Bell, Thunder Smash, 1977, acrylic on canvas, 137.8 × 167.6 cm, CTB.1977.91, Room J, Level 0. Also: Richard Estes, Nedick's, 1970, oil on canvas, 121.9 × 167.6 cm, CTB.1993.10, Room J.
tracks.listen: A pinball machine painted with total precision, and the space-age year that may lie behind its stars.

tracks.title: Out onto the Paseo del Arte
tracks.where: In the central hall by the main entrance on the Paseo del Prado, or just outside the doors on the pavement.
tracks.what: Closing: the walk in review, from Duccio in Room 1 to Pop in Room 52 and the Carmen Thyssen rooms A to J; where to go next on the Paseo del Arte.
tracks.listen: Looking back over two generations and a second collection, and pointing you to the Prado, the Reina Sofía and the Retiro.
